skill.name: codebase-analysis
skill.description: Systematically analyze unfamiliar codebases by discovering entry points, tracing dependencies, identifying architecture patterns, and prioritizing technical debt.
skill.summary: Build an evidence-based map of an unfamiliar codebase before planning changes.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, repository-local discovery commands, and /dev/null redirection. Two intent-level risks remain: a repository-defined npm script and unpinned npx packages can execute untrusted code. No prompt injection, credential access, exfiltration, or suspicious network destination was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval or a sandbox before running npm scripts in unfamiliar repositories. Prefer static coverage configuration inspection first.
Use preinstalled, reviewed tools or pin exact package versions. Add --no-install when downloads are not approved.

semantic_findings.title: Repository-Defined Script Execution
semantic_findings.description: The cookbook recommends npm run test:coverage in unfamiliar repositories. Repository-controlled npm scripts can execute arbitrary commands with the agent's permissions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited command directly invokes an npm script whose implementation is controlled by the repository being analyzed.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned npx Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The cookbooks recommend unpinned npx invocations. npx may download and execute registry packages when the requested tools are absent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Each cited command uses npx without an exact package version or a no-install safeguard.

content.value_statement: Unfamiliar codebases hide entry points, dependencies, architecture, and technical debt. This skill provides a structured workflow for tracing and documenting those elements.
actual_capabilities: Discovers likely entry points across JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Rust, Dart, C, and C++ projects.
Traces imports, exported symbols, module relationships, package dependencies, call paths, and circular dependencies.
Infers architecture patterns from directories, imports, framework conventions, and dependency flow.
Identifies code, test, dependency, documentation, and architecture debt using defined severity levels.
Produces structured reports with overviews, entry points, dependencies, diagrams, and prioritized debt.
limitations: Architecture detection uses heuristics, so conclusions require verification against source behavior.
Shell examples assume common Unix tools and may need adaptation on Windows.
Several debt checks focus on JavaScript and TypeScript, while other languages receive less coverage.
Optional commands can execute repository scripts or download npm packages and require review before use.

use_cases.title: Orient a New Contributor
use_cases.description: Map entry points, framework conventions, and important dependency paths before assigning the first change.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Refactoring Plan
use_cases.description: Trace component boundaries and circular dependencies before changing a fragile subsystem.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Technical Debt
use_cases.description: Build an evidence-based inventory of quality, testing, dependency, documentation, and architecture issues.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Quick Orientation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository at quick depth. Identify its language, framework, configuration files, and main entry points. Cite evidence for every conclusion.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment of an unfamiliar repository

prompt_templates.title: Trace an Entry Point
prompt_templates.prompt: Start from [entry point] and trace direct and transitive dependencies. Highlight external packages, circular references, and uncertain links. Do not modify files.

prompt_templates.title: Review the Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a standard architecture review of [repository]. Detect primary and secondary patterns from structure and imports. Explain conflicting evidence and produce a dependency diagram.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a High-Risk Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a deep analysis of [component]. Map entry points, call paths, ownership boundaries, and debt. Rank refactoring risks and propose verification steps.

output_examples.input: Give me a quick assessment of this TypeScript service.
output: Overview: The project is a TypeScript HTTP service with one application bootstrap and separate route modules.
Entry points: The package manifest identifies the main runtime file, while the server module starts request handling.
Next step: Trace imports from the server module before classifying the architecture.

output_examples.input: Trace dependencies from the authentication service.
output: Direct dependencies: database access, password hashing, token creation, and user lookup modules.
Inbound dependencies: login routes and authentication middleware call the service.
Risk: A circular reference between user lookup and authentication needs source verification.

output_examples.input: Identify and prioritize technical debt before a refactor.
output: High: A large service owns unrelated account, billing, and notification behavior.
Medium: Critical API paths have limited tests and several outdated dependencies.
Recommended order: Add behavior tests, split responsibilities, then update dependencies.

best_practices: Begin with confirmed entry points and trace dependencies outward.
Confirm architecture patterns using both directory structure and import direction.
Request approval before commands that run project scripts or download tools.
anti_patterns: Do not infer architecture from directory names alone.
Do not run package scripts or npx tools in untrusted repositories without approval.
Do not report debt without evidence, locations, severity, and impact.

faq.question: Which languages and frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: The references cover major JavaScript, Python, Go, Java, Rust, Dart, C, C++, and Ruby entry-point conventions.

faq.question: Does the skill modify source files?
faq.answer: The workflow requests analysis and reports, not source edits. Some optional commands can execute project tooling and need approval.

faq.question: Can it generate architecture diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The report format supports dependency diagrams and optional C4 diagrams when requested.

faq.question: How reliable are the architecture conclusions?
faq.answer: They are heuristic conclusions. Verify them against imports, runtime entry points, and source behavior before making design decisions.

faq.question: Which local tools may be needed?
faq.answer: Examples use grep, ripgrep, find, jq, package managers, and optional dependency-analysis tools.

faq.question: Is it suitable for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use read-only inspection first. Skip npm scripts and npx downloads unless a sandbox or explicit approval is available.
